correct_answer: Apply Q2 floor rates ($38/$22) with no exceptions — the rate card explicitly states 'no grandfathering for unsigned proposals' and a verbal commitment has no contractual standing
rationale: The correct answer is B. The rate card cell comment from Rachel Nakamura (approved by CFO) is unambiguous: 'No grandfathering for unsigned proposals.' The proposal was unsigned as of the April 1 effective date, and a verbal commitment at a conference dinner has no contractual standing. NetSuite confirms there is no active contract or signed IO. The policy is clear and there is no established exception mechanism for this situation. Answer A is wrong because an unsigned proposal is not a binding price commitment — the rate card policy specifically anticipated this scenario and closed the loophole. Answer C is wrong because it was suggested informally in a DM (not an official recommendation) and it fundamentally changes what the client wants (majority premium for their EV launch). Restructuring to game the blended rate violates the spirit of the floor while technically complying. Answer D is tempting because it acknowledges the competitive reality, but there is no established 'one-time VP exception' process for rate card floors — Derek's suggestion was speculative ('I think?'). Creating ad hoc exceptions to CFO-approved floors requires more than VP authority and would set a dangerous precedent for every AE with a competing offer from Hulu.
